title: Magic Hash (MHA)
text: Magic Hash (MHA) Magic Hash (MHA) currently circulates as a token on BNB Smart Chain (BSC). The disclosed BSC contract identifies this current token; BSC transactions use BNB for network gas.Planned network rolesWithin the MAGNE network design, MHA is proposed for gas, validator security staking and ecosystem incentives. Migration or integration with MAGNE L1 and M Hash L2 will require a separate announcement covering timing, supported networks, conversion rules and holder actions. Testnet gas tokens are separate from BSC MHA and do not establish migration entitlement.Supply and releaseThe allocation total remains 10,000,000,000 MHA. Release schedules describe distributions from the specified reserve pools, not new issuance above that total. Mining and validator allocations have their own schedules. Any future network fee-burning mechanism requires an explicit implementation specification; it is not a token-price commitment.Governance designThe design also references mBGT for reward coordination and protocol voting. Its retention, transferability and relationship to MHA voting rights remain design decisions to confirm; this does not announce issuance of another token.Contract, reserve addresses and release rules

text: Proof of Work and device rewards What PoW meansProof of Work (PoW) is a consensus approach in which participants perform computational work to compete for block production under the rules of a specific chain. Computational task completion, on its own, is not proof that a device participates in that consensus.How v1.1 uses the term miningGEN1 mining refers to the proposed distribution of the Mining Nodes allocation for eligible device availability and effective tasks. text: Team & Execution Team & Execution MAGNE.AI is developed by a multidisciplinary team spanning secure mobile systems, Web3 infrastructure (L1/L2), security engineering, hardware program execution, and global ecosystem operations. title: Why MAGNE needs Layer 2
text: Why MAGNE needs Layer 2 Separate execution workloadsHigh-frequency applications can compete for limited L1 block space. The L2 design moves application execution and batching to a separate layer while retaining an explicit settlement relationship with L1. This is an architectural objective, not evidence of current production transaction volume.Benefits and dependenciesBatching can share publication costs across transactions.EVM compatibility supports familiar contract tools; it does not guarantee every application works unchanged.Security depends on data availability, settlement verification, sequencing permissions and upgrade controls.A bridge must be explicitly deployed, audited and enabled before assets can move through it.Status and measurementsPublic configurations currently cover MAGNE L1 and M Hash L2 testnets. Mainnet and production settlement are not open. See the official network register for deployment status and parameters.Metrics and assumptions

title: Application security boundaries
text: Application security boundaries From authorisation to executionA secure application must validate user intent, restrict permissions and expose transaction details before signing. Hardware key protection helps protect key material; it does not make an arbitrary contract call safe or remove the need to verify the recipient and requested authority.On-chain recordsRecords can be inspected through the relevant explorer. Their finality depends on the network protocol; upgradeable contracts, privileged operations and off-chain inputs have separate trust assumptions. An audit covers its specified code version and scope, not every future deployment.Operational controlsPublish contract versions and administrative permissions.Monitor incidents, document upgrades and define recovery procedures.Use least-privilege approvals and independently check high-impact transactions.Hardware protection layers

title: M Hash optimisation proposals
text: M Hash optimisation proposals The items below preserve the earlier engineering proposals. Their inclusion does not establish deployment or a measured speed-up. A release claim requires the relevant code change, configuration and reproducible benchmark.Execution layerProposalWhat must be validatedShared intermediate state cache (L1.5)Cache ownership, memory limits, invalidation and reorganisation handling.Diff-layer depth 128 → 32Read amplification, false positives and memory/disk trade-offs under the same workload.originStorage prefetch sharingThread safety, hit rate and consistent state reads.Reuse block execution resultsPayload identity, fork/version compatibility and required revalidation. Engine API versions must match the client.Batch publicationAsynchronous batch submission may reduce waiting between publications, but must track L1 inclusion, replacement and reorganisation recovery. The old “15 confirmations / 45 seconds” example is not a confirmed current setting. Batch submission latency and settlement finality must be measured separately.Acceptance evidenceFor each adopted change, publish the repository and commit, client version, configuration, test workload, before/after measurements and failure-case results. Until then these remain proposals, not published throughput guarantees.

title: Hardware: security and computation
text: Hardware: security and computation MAG1 brings device computation, protected key operations and network access into one product. These roles are distinct; supported features depend on the device, software and application configuration.Three security layersThe official security description references UTEE (CC EAL2+), HyperSeed N60 (CC EAL6+) and HyperSeed 72B (CC EAL6+). These are component or evaluated-scope references, not an EAL rating for the whole phone.HyperSeed N60The secure-element path is designed to keep protected keys inside the hardware and return signatures or authorised results. Actual use depends on the wallet, access rules and user authorisation; not every application transaction automatically follows this path.HyperSeed 72BThe separate NFC recovery design protects recovery material. Recovery access and backup handling must follow the configured procedure. Retention and endurance depend on the applicable component specification and operating conditions.UTEEA trusted execution environment separates designated sensitive operations from ordinary applications. It is a different protection boundary from the secure element.System securityPermission checks, trusted execution, secure signing, software updates and operational testing work together. These controls reduce exposure; they do not promise immunity from malware, malicious approvals or implementation flaws.Certification referencesMAGNE Security · Certification historyThe certificate holder, evaluated version, scope and augmentation apply to the corresponding original document.On-device AILocal inference can reduce dependence on cloud processing for supported workloads. Translation, assistance and detection use cases require their own model, application and device testing; running locally does not by itself establish complete privacy.Network participationWallets and applications can access supported networks. Proposed GEN1 rewards concern eligible device tasks and availability, not automatic L1 validator status or L2 consensus rights.Applications and deliveryApplication availability and device delivery are separate milestones. See the product progress chapter for first-batch delivery and subsequent-batch updates.MAG1 delivery update

title: Gas and fees
text: Gas and fees Gas measures execution work. A transaction fee is not the same as its gas limit or the quoted gas price.Fee componentsIn the proposed L2 design, the fee includes execution gas plus the applicable cost of publishing data to L1. The data component must be estimated through the deployed fee mechanism; it is not obtained by reusing the L2 execution gas quantity. Any additional fee component must be disclosed with its implementation version.L2 total fee = execution gas used × effective gas price + applicable L1 data feeBase fee exampleFor an EIP-1559 block limit of 100M, elasticity of 2 and denominator of 8, the target is 50M gas. At the target the base fee remains unchanged; a full block produces approximately a 12.5% increase. These are illustrative values, not confirmed live settings.Before submitting a transactionConfirm the network and request an estimate from its RPC and wallet.BSC MHA transfers require BNB gas; MAGNE testnets use their own test gas assets.Batching and compression can reduce per-transaction data costs. ZK proofs are not asserted here as an enabled MAGNE fee-reduction mechanism.Measurement assumptions · EIP-1559

toc.title: Does MAGNE use a second governance token?
How fast is M Hash L2?
Is a phone owner automatically a validator?
What are the proposed validator requirements?

text: Frequently asked questions What is MHA?Magic Hash (MHA) currently exists on BSC. Its total allocation is 10 billion. Planned roles in MAGNE-owned networks include gas, security staking and ecosystem incentives; migration terms require a separate announcement.Does MAGNE use a second governance token?The design references mBGT, but its retention and relationship to MHA voting rights remain to be confirmed. This draft neither declares a final single-token governance model nor announces a new token issuance.How fast is M Hash L2?Use dated measurements for the stated network and workload. Earlier 1-second and 2-second claims were not reconciled. Block inclusion, settlement finality and bridge withdrawal time are different metrics. Measurement guideIs a phone owner automatically a validator?No. Device tasks, validator admission and L2 ordering have separate rules. GEN1 eligibility does not grant block-production rights.What are the proposed validator requirements?The earlier proposal specified 250,000–10,000,000 MHA per validator, suitable server resources and availability checks. Admission, selection, penalties and the final consensus model require a confirmed technical specification before activation.Where do validator rewards come from?The 15% Staking Nodes allocation is separate from the 30% Mining Nodes allocation. Its earlier schedule releases half of that pool in year one and halves the annual amount thereafter. Eligibility and weighting must follow its own final rules. Staking allocationDoes a phone receive 20,000 MHA in any 24 months?No. The illustration assumes participation from network M1, a fixed eligible population no greater than 13,750, full availability/effective work, and the standard base release schedule. Late entry and changing device counts change the result.What is PoL?Proof of Liquidity is a proposed way to coordinate eligible liquidity participation and reward allocation. It must not be treated as a complete consensus specification by itself. The deployed vault rules determine eligibility, release and claims.Do liquidity deposits automatically earn rewards?Not necessarily. Pool fees and additional vault incentives are separate. Vault admission, eligible receipt assets, funded budget and claim requirements must be checked for the actual deployment.What is a DEX or liquidity pool?A DEX uses smart contracts to support asset exchange. A liquidity pool holds assets under its contract rules; price impact depends on pool design, depth and trade size. Swap fees, network gas and slippage are different costs.How do APR and APY differ?APR is an annualised rate without compounding; APY includes an assumed compounding schedule. Neither is a guaranteed return. Fee income, incentives and asset-value changes must be distinguished.Can holders vote now?This draft does not establish a live governor. The voting asset, delegation method, contract and start date must be published before voting instructions apply. Governance proposal

title: Glossary
text: Glossary Terms used in this draftMHA / Magic HashCurrent BSC token; total allocation 10 billion. Future MAGNE network uses are proposals until enabled.mBGTDesign reference for reward coordination and protocol voting; retention, issuance and its relation to MHA remain to be confirmed.MagneKitProject framework name in earlier material. Its client implementation, consensus engine and release version require technical confirmation.CometBFTA Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus engine. Mentioning it in a design does not establish that a MAGNE network runs it.ConsensusRules by which nodes agree on accepted blocks and state. Separate from reward budgeting and device-task verification.PoWProof of Work: a consensus family using computational competition. Not a synonym for any rewarded computation.PoLProof of Liquidity: a proposed liquidity-participation and reward-allocation mechanism in this design.PoAI / GEN1Device-work design and first-generation device reward programme. Eligibility, budget and release are specified in Tokenomics.Validator / sequencerValidator responsibilities follow L1 consensus; a sequencer orders L2 transactions. Neither role is automatically granted by owning a phone.Block / block timeA block records transactions and state commitments. Block time must identify the chain and observation period.Execution client / Engine APIAn execution client processes state transitions. Engine API connects execution with the applicable consensus or rollup component; supported versions depend on the release.Finality / withdrawal periodFinality describes when a chain accepts a state as final under its security model. A bridge withdrawal may have a separate challenge or processing period.Single-slot finalityFinalisation within a slot under a specific protocol. This glossary does not assert that MAGNE implements it.Staking / delegationStaking subjects assets to specific protocol rules. Delegation can assign voting or validation weight; it is not necessarily an asset transfer and must identify the governing contract.GovernanceProposal, review, voting and execution of changes under stated authority. The voting asset and deployed governance status must be explicit.DEX / MagneSwapA decentralised exchange supports swaps through contracts. MagneSwap remains a planned project application in this draft.Liquidity / pool / LPLiquidity is executable market depth. Pools hold assets under contract rules; liquidity providers bear the applicable price and contract risks.Reward vaultA contract arrangement for eligible assets and funded incentives. Admission, rates and claim rules depend on its deployed version.Released / disbursed / claimableReserve release makes budget available under its schedule. Disbursement uses an approved budget. Claimable amounts have met the recipient release conditions. These are not interchangeable balances.Testnet / mainnetTestnet assets and records serve testing. Production/mainnet status requires a separate launch; testnet availability does not establish production settlement.
